column1: # The order of the identity and rights checks of a request at a door of the store (P/01.2 N3 «check»). The norm refers to this table and does not repeat it in prose.
# The input is one request of a store door of chapters 1.1 and 1.2 (a daemon of a group or a box); body is the request object below, not the JSON body of the request.
# Rows in the order of n: the first row whose when is true gives the refusal code, kind and the fields fault; none — the request goes on to its operation. The table does not read the store state.
# Before the table: the frame and the body limit (P/01.1 N2.1, R217 of P/01.1), the route and the method of the door (404 — P/01.1 N2.1); for GET /v1/get and GET /v1/list
# the rows 1–4 of forms/read-checks.tsv (the form of the query and the key rules: N3 «read» of P/01.1 step 1 before step 2 «check»); POST /v1/write comes to the table
# before its body is parsed and goes on after row 3 to the form of its body and to forms/write-checks.tsv, whose rows wc-rights, wc-guard_rights, wc-write_rights
# and wc-guard_elem_rights (n 14, 15, 33, 34) are the write, delete and guard rights of this check; they are not repeated here.
# Outside the table, between rows 2 and 3: the ban on a forwarded admin while a rights file is loaded (forwarding_untrusted, P/01.2 N3 «check»).
# GET /v1/list has no row of the read right: after the identity the names and versions are given without it. GET /v1/rights while no rights file is loaded — 404 (P/01.2 N2), not a row of this table.
# On a box there are no trusted forwarding senders and no peers (P/01.2 N1.1): there a role header on any socket is the refusal of row 1.
# op — * in every row: the request object has no field op. when and fault are CEL (extensions strings, two-var-comprehensions; type(), has(), matches() — standard CEL). Variables:

#var body dyn — the request object {method, path, query, size, role_header}: method — the HTTP method; path — the target before ?, byte for byte; query — the pairs of the query by P/01.1 N2.1, a map from a name to the list of its values in order; size — the number of bytes of the HTTP body (of chunked — the decoded bytes); role_header — the value of the role forwarding header, null without the header

#var sock string — the role of the socket or of the transport: <role> of <role>.sock, admin of admin.sock, on a box — the writer's name; for a connection over -api — peer: and the role in the SAN of the verified certificate of the peer (peer:configstore — a voter, peer:configstore-door — the door without a vote)
#var lone list<string> — not read by this table: the request object carries no strings of a JSON body
#var lim map<string,int> — the parameters of the lesson, only the names of #lim; this table has none

#fn allowed(string, string, string) -> bool — full permission for the effective role, operation read | write | delete and key by P/01.2 N3 «check», including never and admin/internal-role exceptions; not only the ordinary-role file evaluator
# The effective role of rows 3 and 4: role_header, when the header is present and sock is peer:configstore or peer:configstore-door; otherwise sock.
# id — the stable address of the row: rc-<check>, apart from the order n; not renumbered

column7: body.path == "/v1/rights" && (body.role_header != null && sock in ["peer:configstore", "peer:configstore-door"] ? body.role_header : sock) != "admin"
body.path == "/v1/get" && !allowed((body.role_header != null && sock in ["peer:configstore", "peer:configstore-door"] ? body.role_header : sock), "read", body.query.key[0])
